      "observations": [
        "The complete one-path landing adds Timer.setTimeout and a handler-owned counter. It awaits addTargetCalendarItem and then, after ten normally completed add calls, awaits a zero-delay timer and resets the counter. There is no surrounding catch at this landing: an add rejection prevents its counter increment. The listener exception already allows processing unchanged ETags.",
        "Current multiget processing enters the add branch for new items, changed ETags, or an explicit listener. The counter increments after the addTargetCalendarItem try/catch, so failed additions are logged but still count toward yielding. Unchanged ETags without a listener skip this branch; delete responses and unexpected-response branches do not increment this counter.",
        "The multiget request batch preference defaults to100 and limits server-request hrefs. Its10-attempt UI-yield threshold is a separate control. The separately inspected WebDav sync response loop yields at25 handled response branches. Neither threshold is a universal CalDAV performance rule or measured responsiveness guarantee.",
        "The old focused lessons described completed additions/changed items too narrowly. The correction preserves the handler boundary while naming attempted additions, catch continuation and the explicit-listener exception. No new regression test or benchmark is added by this landing.",

Queue/token/caller ownership claims in that record are not re-audited or superseded here.",

The landing expands the comment to name UI blocking, uncached calendars and start-up delay, despite the thread remaining NotDone.
